rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He supplies an omitted condition: if their claim were true, they should compose a comparable surah, since they too possess Arabic eloquence and rhetorical skill.
rows.anchor: فقال: قل إن كان الأمر كما تزعمون فأتوا أنتم على وجه الافتراء بسورة مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in مثله refers to the Quran, so the challenge is to produce a surah comparable to it; Abū Ḥayyān refers readers to his earlier account of inimitability.
rows.anchor: والضمير في مثله عائد على القرآن أي: بسورة مماثلة للقرآن

rows.speaker: عمرو بن قائد
rows.claim: He reads بسورة مثله as a genitive construction: a surah of a book or speech like the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمرو بن قائد بسورة مثله على الإضافة أي: بسورة كتاب أو كلام مثله

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: He treats the wording as an adjective standing for an omitted noun such as a human being like the Prophet; the mainstream reading instead refers to the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح: هذا مما حذف الموصوف منه وأقيمت الصفة مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challengers are told to enlist any created beings other than God, since only God can produce its like; this tests their claim that the Prophet invented it.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر على أن يأتي بمثله أحد إلا الله

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They infer that the Quran is created: a challenge to produce its like assumes that such production is possible in principle, whereas matching an eternal thing would be impossible.
rows.anchor: وقد تمسك المعتزلة بهذه الآية على خلق القرآن قالوا: لأنه تحدى به

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: He counts six challenge levels: the whole Quran, ten surahs, one surah, a comparable discourse, one surah from anyone learned or unlearned, and collective effort; the first four require a Prophet-like untrained opponent, while the fifth addresses individuals and the last a group.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: مراتب التحدي بالقرآن ست تحد بكل القرآن في: قل لئن اجتمعت الآية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The deniers hastened to reject the Quran on first hearing, before understanding or reflecting on it, from aversion to what opposed their inherited religion.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: بل كذبوا، بل سارعوا إلى التكذيب بالقرآن، وفاجأوه في بديهة السماع قبل أن يفهموه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: One reading takes what they lacked knowledge of as the threatened punishment and its outcome, making the verse a warning; another takes it as the Quran, whose unseen content, arrangement, and explanation they did not yet know.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: هذا اللفظ يحتمل معنيين: أحدهما: أن يريد بما الوعيد الذي توعدهم الله على الكفر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says they called Quranic narratives old tales before grasping their purpose and lesson.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: يحتمل وجوها، الأول: كلما سمعوا شيئا من القصص قالوا أساطير الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of al-Razi's argument says the narratives teach that God reverses fortunes and ends worldly life as a lesson, and that an untrained Messenger received them by revelation without distortion.
rows.anchor: أهله من عز إلى ذل، ومن ذل إلى عز، وبفناء الدنيا، فيعتبر بذلك. وأن ذلك القصص بوحي من الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: They heard the disconnected letters without understanding and formed a bad opinion; God answered elsewhere that the scripture contains clear signs.
rows.anchor: الثاني: كلما سمعوا خروف التهجي ولم يفهموا منها شيئا ساء ظنهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: They objected that the Quran came gradually rather than all at once, an objection answered elsewhere in the Quran.
rows.anchor: الثالث: ظهور القرآن شيئا فشيئا، فساء ظنهم وقالوا: لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: They rejected resurrection because they knew only sensory things, while the Quran establishes return to life with many proofs.
rows.anchor: الرابع: القرآن مملوء من الحشر، وكانوا ألفوا المحسوسات، فاستبعدوا حصول الحياة بعد الموت

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: They objected to worship commands on the ground that God needs no obedience; the Quran answers that good deeds benefit their doers.
rows.anchor: الخامس: أنه مملوء من الأمر بالعبادات، وكانوا يقولون: إله العالم غني عن طاعتنا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: In summary, they denied matters whose reality and wisdom they had not grasped; the verse also faults their failure to investigate the Quran's secrets.
rows.anchor: فقوله: بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه، إشارة إلى عدم علمهم بهذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains لَمَّا as anticipating later recognition: first they denied without reflection, then, after repeated challenges exposed their inability, they persisted from envy and rebellion; Abū Ḥayyān says this needs scrutiny.
rows.anchor: ويحتاج كلامه هذا إلى نظر. وقال أيضا: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Quran's predictions had not yet come to pass, so they denied before testing either its literary inimitability or the truth of its unseen reports; Abū Ḥayyān notes a subtle grammatical distinction remains to be explained.
rows.anchor: ولم يأتهم بعد تأويل ما فيه من الإخبار بالغيوب أي عاقبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison says earlier peoples likewise denied before considering prophetic miracles fairly, following their ancestors; الظالمين most naturally refers to those earlier peoples, possibly the present deniers.
rows.anchor: يعني: قبل النظر في معجزات الأنبياء وقبل تدبرها من غير إنصاف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: As quoted by Ibn ʿAṭiyya, كيف is the predicate of كان and cannot be governed by انظر because an interrogative blocks a preceding governor.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: قال الزجاج: كيف، في موضع نصب على خبر كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the asserted blanket rule: كيف has interrogative and conditional uses, and in either construction the syntax must be analyzed according to its actual function.
rows.anchor: ليس كما ذكر، بل لكيف معنيان: أحدهما: الاستفهام المحض

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests كيف may function like an abstract noun in examples such as كن كيف شئت; Abū Ḥayyān rejects deriving the noun كيفية as its source.
rows.anchor: وقوله: ولكيف تصرفات إلى آخره، ليس كيف تحل محل المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In كن كيف شئت, كيف is conditional and its answer is omitted: be as you wish; the parallel قم متى شئت likewise omits an answer recoverable from the preceding command.
rows.anchor: وأما كن كيف شئت، فكيف ليست بمعنى كيفية، وإنما هي شرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bukhari's heading كيف كان بدء الوحي is a plain interrogative, perhaps quoting a question and then answering it with the narration.
rows.anchor: وأما قول البخاري: كيف كان بدء الوحي؟ فهو استفهام محض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الظالمين apparently refers to the people before them, but can also refer back to those who denied the Quran in this passage.
rows.anchor: والظالمين: الظاهر أنه أريد به الذين من قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparently some Quraysh disbelievers will later believe because they are destined for felicity, while others will die persisting in disbelief.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه إخبار بأن من كفار قريش من سيؤمن به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, among those who remain unbelievers, some inwardly know the Quran is true but deny it stubbornly, while others reject it inwardly and outwardly, from haste or unresolved doubts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو تقسيم في الكفار الباقين على كفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This division shows that the deniers are not uniform in belief; they are internally divided even though all share public rejection.
rows.anchor: وفيه تفريق كلمة الكفار، وأنهم ليسوا مستوين في اعتقاداتهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the pronoun in ومنهم to refer to the People of the Book, though its apparent antecedent is the people denoted by أم يقولون.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في ومنهم عائد على أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singling out God's knowledge of the corrupters is a grave threat to them.
rows.anchor: وتعلق العلم بالمفسدين وحدهم تهديد عظيم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If denial continues, the Prophet is to disavow them after delivering his message; each party bears the recompense of its deeds, his righteous faith and obedience versus their idolatry and disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي وإن تمادوا على تكذيبك فتبرأ منهم قد أعذرت وبلغت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is apparently a disavowal, truce, and warning; another view says its aim is to draw them in and reconcile them.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها آية منابذة لهم وموادعة، وضمنها الوعيد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd, along with Mujahid, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil, regards this Meccan verse as abrogated by the command to fight; the investigating scholars reject abrogation because the sword verse does not remove individual responsibility and recompense.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم منهم ابن زيد: هي منسوخة بالقتال لأنها مكية، وهو قول: مجاهد

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: They deny abrogation: the verse assigns each person their own acts and their consequences of reward or punishment, which the fighting verses do not cancel.
rows.anchor: وقال المحققون: ليست بمنسوخة، ومدلولها اختصاص كل واحد بأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order puts my work first to stress separation, then completes the parallel with your work; it also preserves the verse ending and cadence.
rows.anchor: وبدأ في المأمور بقوله: لي عملي لأنه آكد في الانتفاء منهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the two verses were revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith and other mockers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت الآيتان في النضر بن الحرث وغيره من المستهزئين

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari instead says they concern a group of Jews.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: في قوم من اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses divide unbelievers into listeners who are deaf to meaning and viewers who are blind to evidence; plural agreement first follows the sense of من and singular agreement later follows its grammatical form.
rows.anchor: والعود على المعنى دون العود على اللفظ في الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their listening brings no understanding or acceptance: deafness is compounded by lack of reason, whereas a rational deaf person can still find guidance through thought.
rows.anchor: هم، وإن استمعوا إليك صم عن إدراك ما تلقيه إليهم ليس لهم وعي ولا قبول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot be guided because they lack sight and insight; unlike an ordinary blind person who may infer things through inner perception, they have lost both.
rows.anchor: لأن السبب الذي يهتدى به إلى رؤية الدلائل قد فقدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired images intensify the impossibility of acceptance by combining deafness with absent reason and blindness with absent insight.
rows.anchor: جمعوا بين الصمم وانتفاء العقل، وبين العمى وفقد البصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions console the Prophet and tell him not to grieve over their refusal, since guidance belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وقوله: أفأنت؟ تسلية للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says a verb can follow the meaning of من after a first verb follows its grammatical form, but not in the reverse order; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this restriction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: جاء ينظر على لفظ من، وإذا جاء الفعل على لفظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says either agreement pattern can follow the other: the speaker may first follow meaning and then grammatical form, with further details left to grammar.
rows.anchor: بل يجوز أن تراعي المعنى أولا فتعيد الضمير على حسب ما تريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' extreme hostility makes them like deaf fools and blind people without insight, unable to appreciate eloquence, Quranic inimitability, or the miracles God gives the Messenger; their guidance is hopeless.
rows.anchor: بأن هؤلاء الكفار قد انتهوا في النفرة والعداوة والبغض الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A quoted poet compares the inability to perceive hidden excellence to a blind eye that cannot see; the poet is unnamed in the passage.
rows.anchor: وإذا خفيت على المعني فعاذر ... أن لا تراءى مقلة عمياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not wrong people: He removed their excuses through messengers and warnings, while they wrong themselves through disbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: إذ قد أزاح عللهم ببعثة الرسل وتحذيرهم من عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of injustice may concern worldly interests, or the afterlife punishment, which is just because they acquired the sins under God's decree; God is not questioned about His acts.
rows.anchor: واحتمل هذا النفي للظلم أن يكون في الدنيا أي: لا يظلمهم شيئا من مصالحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes an earlier discussion of readings that either double the nūn with الناس accusative or lighten it with الناس nominative.
rows.anchor: وتقدم خلاف القراء في، ولكن الناس من تشديد النون ونصب الناس وتخفيفها والرفع

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ḥafṣ read يحشرهم with yāʾ, making God the unspoken subject in continuity with the preceding mention of God.
rows.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وحفص: يحشرهم بالياء راجعا الضمير غائبا عائدا على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrected will feel their worldly life or time in the graves lasted only briefly, either because of the terrors they see or the long day and its accounting.
rows.anchor: كأن لم يلبثوا في الدنيا أو في القبور يعني: فقليل لبثهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they view their long lifetimes as an hour when compared with eternity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: رأوا أن طول أعمارهم في مقابلة الخلود كساعة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers several parses for يوم: an implicit command to remember, an implied verb of swiftness, or the verb يتعارفون; he also suggests the comparison may modify the day, a source noun, or the object pronoun.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويوم ظرف، ونصبه يصح بفعل مضمر تقديره: واذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān finds Ibn ʿAṭiyya's implied swiftness analysis unexplained, and rejects making the comparison an adjective of the definite day: the clause describes the resurrected, not the day.
rows.anchor: أما قوله: ويصح أن ينتصب بالفعل الذي يتضمنه كأن لم يلبثوا فإنه كلام مجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes كأن لم يلبثوا a circumstantial clause attached to the object pronoun of نحشرهم, as Zamakhshari and Abu al-Baqa also parse it.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أنها جملة حالية من مفعول نحشرهم كما قاله ابن عطية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He parses كأن لم يلبثوا as a state of the resurrected; يتعارفون either modifies the time as a circumstance or explains that recognition persists for a while before turning into mutual denial.
rows.anchor: أما الأولى فحال منهم أي: نحشرهم مشبهين بمن لم يلبث إلا ساعة

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfi parses يتعارفون as a circumstantial future participle from يلبثوا or as a circumstance of نحشرهم.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: يتعارفون فعل مستقبل في موضع الحال من الضمير في يلبثوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed source-noun parse requires an omitted قبله to link the comparison to the noun, but Abū Ḥayyān says deleting this connector is impermissible.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكرنا أن حذف مثل هذا الرابط لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parsers allow يتعارفون to be a circumstantial clause, or an independent report that recognition occurs between them.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون جملة مستأنفة، أخبر تعالى أنه يقع التعارف بينهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says they recognize each other as they did in life when leaving their graves, but the recognition is blame and exposure rather than affection, then ends amid the terrors of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يعرف بعضهم بعضا كمعرفتهم في الدنيا إذا خرجوا من قبورهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says they recognize one another's former error and disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعرف بعضهم بعضا ما كانوا عليه من الخطأ والكفر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets recognition as the believers showing mutual affection, while unbelievers have no family ties among them.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: تعارف تعاطف المؤمنين، والكافرون لا أنساب بينهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says resurrection has different stations: people recognize each other in some and not in others.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القيامة مواطن، ففي موطن يتعارفون وفي موطن لا يتعارفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that the deniers lost is apparently an independent report; Zamakhshari calls it an exclamation or a statement spoken during their recognition.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: قد خسر الذين إلى آخره جملة مستأنفة

rows.speaker: مجاهِد
rows.claim: Mujahid and others say the judgment is future: the messenger will witness against his people, then God will judge them fairly, sending some to Paradise and others to Hell.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاءهم رسولهم يوم القيامة للشهادة عليهم قضي بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the judgment as occurring in this world, with the messenger saved and the deniers punished; the future interpretation concerns judgment on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: بين الرسول وأمته، فأنجى الرسول وعذب المكذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh ask when the promised punishment will come to dismiss or mock it; their claim that the messengers are truthful is sarcastic and supports reading the earlier judgment as a past worldly event.
rows.anchor: استعجلوا بما وعدوا به من العذاب على سبيل الاستبعاد، أو على سبيل الاستخفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet cannot independently bring harm or benefit even to himself, he cannot control their punishment or know its timing without God's disclosure; God alone knows each community's appointed term.
rows.anchor: ليس ذلك إلي، بل ذلك إلى الله تعالى. وإذا كنت لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sīrīn reads آجالهم in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن سيرين: آجالهم على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception ما شاء الله can be connected: except what God wills him to control; the appointed term is a fixed time for their punishment.
rows.anchor: ظاهره أنه استثناء متصل، إلا ما شاء الله أن أملكه وأقدر عليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari treats the exception as disconnected: rather, whatever God wills will occur, so the Prophet cannot bring harm or punishment himself.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هو استثناء منقطع أي: ولكن ما شاء الله من ذلك كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following question challenges criminals who demand punishment to say what part of it they would hasten if it arrived by night or day.
rows.anchor: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāʾaytum means tell me and normally takes two objects; here its first object is omitted in a contest of governors, and the second is the interrogative clause. The omitted first object is not resumed because that usage is rare or poetic.
rows.anchor: أرأيت زيدا ما صنع: المعنى: أخبرني عن زيد ما صنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is to ask what they would hasten from God's punishment; since all punishment is bitter and repellent, the question gently warns them against asking for it.
rows.anchor: وليس شيء من العذاب يستعجله عاقل، إذا العذاب كله مر المذاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question expresses astonishment at the severity and horror of the punishment they demand.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الجملة جاءت على سبيل التعجب والتهويل للعذاب

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfi treats رؤية as inward knowledge, takes the question as confirmation, and says the conditional answer is omitted; Abū Ḥayyān notes he does not explain the omitted answer.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: الرؤية من رؤية القلب التي بمعنى العلم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari connects the question to أرأيتم and supplies the missing answer: they would regret having hurried and recognize their mistake; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this estimate as syntactically unsound.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف: وهو تندموا على الاستعجال وتعرفوا الخطأ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān's viable reconstruction is: if punishment comes, tell me what the criminals would be hastening from.
rows.anchor: فالذي يسوغ أن يقدر إن أتاكم عذابه فأخبروني ماذا يستعجل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari proposes that the question is parenthetical and the later question about believing when punishment arrives answers the condition; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because an interrogative conditional answer requires fāʾ and because the clause cannot fill أرأيتم's object.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون اعتراضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بياَتا means punishment comes while people sleep or are occupied with livelihood; a sudden attack is harsher than one for which they prepared, as in the Quran's paired examples.
rows.anchor: والمعنى إن أتاكم عذابه وأنتم ساهون غافلون، إما بنوم وإما باشتغال بالمعاش والكسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ماذا may split into ما as subject and ذا as a relative predicate with an omitted object, or form one object meaning what; a further subject parse is weakened by lacking a linking pronoun. منه apparently refers to punishment, though a view refers it to God.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عود الضمير في منه على العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the threatened event is true; its pronoun may refer to punishment, the law and Quran, the warning, or the Hour.
rows.anchor: وأحق هو الضمير عائد على العذاب. وقيل: على الشرع والقرآن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari construes يستنبئونك as taking one object in the quoted question, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats it as asking the Prophet and suspending its second object in an indirect question.
rows.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: بيقولون أحق هو فجعل يستنبئونك تتعدى إلى واحد

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says استنبأ can govern two objects, the second introduced by عن, and the question here suspends the second object; his alternative derives it from يستعلم and posits three objects.
rows.anchor: وأصل استنبأ أن يتعدى إلى مفعولين: أحدهما بعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects the three-object analysis because استعلم is not attested as taking three objects; merely glossing the verb as ask for knowledge does not add that valency.
rows.anchor: وليس كما ذكر، لأن استعلم لا يحفظ كونها متعدية إلى مفاعيل ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary parse makes هو the subject and حق its predicate; an alternative makes حق the subject and هو its agent, but حق is a verbal noun rather than an active or passive participle, though it can mean established.
rows.anchor: وارتفع هو على أنه مبتدأ، وحق خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is taunting and denying; al-Aʿmash reads الحق, making the sarcasm stronger by contrasting the alleged truth with falsehood.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستفهام منهم على جهة الاستهزاء والإنكار. وقرأ الأعمش: الحق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari says the definite article in الأحق invokes the category of truth, as if asking whether this is truth rather than falsehood or the thing they call true.
rows.anchor: لتضمنه معنى التعريض بأنه باطل، وذلك أن اللام للجنس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says إي is used only in oaths and can be joined to the oath wāw, not spoken alone; Abū Ḥayyān denies that later colloquial speech is valid linguistic evidence.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة فيما سمعه الزمخشري من ذلك لعدم الحجية في كلامه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says إي means yes, precedes an oath, and may occur with or without the oath particle, as in إي ربي and إي وربي.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: هي لفظة تتقدم القسم، وهي بمعنى نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is ordered to answer yes by his Lord: the warning is truly real and they cannot escape God.
rows.anchor: وأمر تعالى نبيه أن يقول مجيبا لهم: قل إي وربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent construction has two clauses: tell them to rejoice in God's grace and mercy, then repeats the command for emphasis, with an omitted verb in the first clause.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته، فبذلك فليفرحوا جملتان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari takes the repetition as emphasis and restricts proper rejoicing to these gifts; the fa implies a condition, or the command may mean to attend to and rejoice in them, or rejoice at their arrival.
rows.anchor: والتكرير للتقرير والتأكيد، وإيجاب اختصاص الفضل والرحمة بالفرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says there is no evidence for inserting اعتنوا; if the phrase modifies the arrival of admonition, the omitted connection belongs after قل rather than across it.
rows.anchor: أما إضمار فليعنتوا فلا دليل عليه

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfi connects the preposition to the implied meaning: the admonition came by God's grace.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: الباء متعلقة بما دل على المعنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the first fa is extra and thereby makes بذلك a substitute for the preceding grace and mercy; another view treats the second fa as emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الفاء الأولى زائدة، ويكون بذلك بدلا مما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejoicing in God's grace and mercy does not conflict with the ban on exultation: joy is praised when directed to faith, reward, and good works, and blamed when directed to worldly wealth, pride, or ingratitude.
rows.anchor: وإنما يمدح الفرح ويذم بحسب متعلقه

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: A number of early authorities, including ʿUthmān, Ubayy, Anas, al-Ḥasan, and others, read فلتفرحوا with second-person address; this is also reported from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عثمان بن عفان، وأبي، وأنس، والحسن، وأبو رجاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributes the addressed reading فلتفرحوا وتجمعون to Ubayy, Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and al-Ḥasan, citing Harun's claim; Abū Ḥayyān corrects the reading attributed to Ibn ʿĀmir.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وقرأ أبي وابن القعقاع، وابن عامر، والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical majority reads فليفرحوا as a third-person command; in the Seven, Ibn ʿĀmir has that form while reading تجمعون with second-person address, unlike the other Seven.
rows.anchor: والجمهور بالياء على أمر الغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy's codex has فبذلك فافرحوا, the common direct imperative, while the third-person command is a less common Arabic form; al-Ḥasan and Abu al-Tayyah read the lām with kasra.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي: فبذلك فافرحوا، وهذه هي اللغة الكثيرة الشهيرة في أمر المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular هو and ذلك indicate that grace and mercy are two names for one thing; what people gather means the debris and comforts of worldly life.
rows.anchor: على أنهما شيء واحد عبر عنه باسمين على سبيل التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وما تكون في شأنه, the pronoun may refer to the Prophet's affair, to the Quran as the most important part of that affair, to revelation (each part being Quran), or to God as the source of every recitation.
rows.anchor: ومن قرآن تفسير للضمير، وخص من العموم لأن القرآن هو أعظم شؤونه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in ولا تعملون is general, as is the statement of divine witness; the preceding activities describe habitual states, while إذ sets the witness in past time and turns the present verb into a past sense.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت الأفعال السابقة المراد بها الحالة الدائمة وتنسحب على الأفعال الماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God switches from the Prophet to his community in ولا تعملون to warn them, although His witnessing encompasses all creation; the following singular address to the Prophet honors him.
rows.anchor: عدل عن خطابه صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى خطاب أمته بقوله: ولا تعملون من عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb تفيضون is explained with several close senses: to engage, spread, push, proceed, take up, convey, speak, or strive.
rows.anchor: وتفيضون: تخوضون، أو تنشرون، أو تدفعون، أو تنهضون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is mentioned before heaven because it is where the hearers live, unlike the usual order in other verses.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر شهادته تعالى على أعمال الخلق ناسب تقديم الأرض الذي هي محل المخاطبين

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Muṣrif, and al-Kisāʾī read يعزب with kasra on the zāy, as in Saba.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب، والأعمش، وابن مصرف، والكسائي، يعزب بكسر الزاي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثقال is a noun meaning the weight of a particle; ذر are tiny ants, used as the smallest familiar breeding creature and a figure for the least thing.
rows.anchor: والمثقال اسم لا صفة، ومعناه هنا وزن ذرة. والذر صغار النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse moves from the smallest to the largest: if God knows the tiniest hidden thing, His knowledge necessarily encompasses the greatest.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى أنه لا يغيب عن علمه أدق الأشياء التي نشاهدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers put fatḥ on both rāʾs, coordinating them to ذرة or مثقال by form; Ḥamza raises them, coordinating to the syntactic position of مثقال because من is extra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر بفتح الراء فيهما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari, following al-Zajjaj, prefers the accusative as a universal negation or the nominative as a new subject.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري تابعا لاختيار الزجاج: والوجه النصب على نفي الجنس، والرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa resolves the awkward exception as disconnected: rather, it is in a clear book.
rows.anchor: وخرجه أبو البقاء على أنه استثناء منقطع تقديره: لكن هو في كتاب مبين

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi quotes two answers: the exception is disconnected, or remoteness means distance in the causal hierarchy; every particle and its known form are nevertheless written in a clear book.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: أجاب بعض المحققين من وجهين

rows.speaker: الجرجاني صاحب النظم
rows.claim: Al-Jurjani says إلا can mean و, citing Quranic examples; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because Arabic usage does not establish إلا as a conjunction.
rows.anchor: وقال الجرجاني صاحب النظم: إلا بمعنى الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says Zamakhshari's objection rests on an invalid estimate of the coordinated exception, which would make the statement say that the thing disappears into the book.
rows.anchor: وإنما أشكل عنده، لأن التقدير يصير إلا في كتاب فيعزب، وهذا كلام لا يصح

none: Quranic verse text only; no commentary points occur in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening continues a discussion of the reading of لِيُضِلُّوا, noting a fatḥ reading and al-Shaʿbī's kasra reading, with an intermediate vowel variant.
rows.anchor: بفتحها. وقرأ الشعبي بكسرها، والى بين الكسرات الثلاث

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī posits an omitted لا, yielding the sense so they would not lead people astray from God's path.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لا محذوفة، التقدير لئلا يضلوا عن سبيلك قاله: أبو علي الجبائي

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرقاشي
rows.claim: Abu al-Faḍl al-Raqāshī reads أإنك آتيت as a question.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الفضل الرقاشي: أإنك آتيت على الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because wealth was their most prized possession, Moses prayed for it to be blotted out, meaning effaced, altered, or destroyed.
rows.anchor: ولما تقدم ذكر الأموال وهي أعز ما ادخر دعا بالطموس عليها وهي التعفية والتغيير أو الإهلاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb say the coins and mines became inscribed stones, including complete, half, and third coins, leaving no usable ore.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومحمد بن كعب: صارت دراهمهم حجارة منقوشة صحاحا وأثلاثا وأنصافا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the wealth and crops became stone.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: بلغنا أن أموالهم وزروعهم صارت حجارة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and ʿAṭiyya say the wealth was destroyed until it could no longer be seen.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعطية: أهلكها حتى لا ترى

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says their land, coins, furnishings, and everything they owned became stones.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أرض دنانيرهم ودراهمهم وفرشهم وكل شيء لهم حجارة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb recounts telling ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz that a find from Egypt contained fruits and coins that were actually stones.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: سألني عمر بن عبد العزيز فذكرت ذلك له

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Abu Ṣāliḥ, and al-Qurṭubī say their sugar became stone.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، والقرطبي: جعل سكرهم حجارة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says fruits, date palms, and food were transformed into stone.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: مسخ الله الثمار والنخل والأطعمة حجارة

rows.speaker: ابن النقيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Naqīb transmits from pious travelers who claimed to see Egyptian stones shaped like coins, fruits, vegetables, and trees.
rows.anchor: أخبرني جماعة من الصالحين كان شغلهم السياحة أنهم عاينوا بجبال مصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Muqātil, al-Farrāʾ, and al-Zajjāj explain شُدَّدْ as sealing the hearts and preventing belief; another report from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk says to destroy them as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومقاتل والفراء والزجاج اطبع عليها وامنعها من الأيمان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the prayer as asking God to make their hearts firm in error.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: اشدد عليها بالضلالة

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses the prayer as harden their hearts.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: قس قلوبهم

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Baḥr interprets it as asking for their hearts to be struck with death.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: اشدد عليها بالموت

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmānī says they should find no consolation for losing their wealth and no patience to bear its disappearance.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني: أي لا يجدوا سلوا عن أموالهم، ولا صبرا على ذهابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group reads اطمس with ḍamma on the mīm, a recognized dialectal form.
rows.anchor: اطمس بضم الميم، وهي لغة مشهورة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: The jussive فلا يؤمنوا is a prayer according to al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, supported by a line of al-Aʿshā; other parses make it a subjunctive result of the prayer or coordinated with لِيُضِلُّوا.
rows.anchor: فلا يؤمنوا مجزوم على أنه دعاء عند الكسائي والفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the punishment is the terminal point because faith then brings no benefit and cannot remove disbelief; the painful punishment was their drowning.
rows.anchor: وكأن رؤية العذاب غاية ونهاية، لأن الإيمان إذ ذاك لا ينفع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās transmits from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb that Moses prayed and Aaron said amen, so the supplication is attributed to both; both may also have prayed, while the singular-as-dual explanation is unlikely.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: قال محمد بن كعب: كان موسى يدعو وهارون يؤمن

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the answer did not become visible until forty years later; they were told their supplication coincided with what was decreed, which counts as an answer.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن جريج، ومحمد بن علي، والضحاك: أن الدعوة لم تظهر إجابتها إلا بعد أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to follow those ignorant of God's ways tells Moses and Aaron not to demand that God's decree be hastened, since His promise cannot fail.
rows.anchor: أي في أن تستعجلا قضائي، فإن وعدي لا خلف له

rows.speaker: السلمي
rows.claim: Al-Sulamī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read دعواتكما in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي والضحاك: دعواتكما على الجمع

rows.speaker: ابن السميقع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa reads قد أُجِيبَتْ دعوتكما as a completed report; al-Rabīʿ reads دعوتيكما, supporting the view that Aaron also prayed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميقع: قد أجبت دعوتكما خبرا عن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the answer, Moses and Aaron are commanded to persist in steadfastness, continue their mission, call people to God, and establish God's proof.
rows.anchor: ثم أمرا بالاستقامة، والمعنى: الديمومة عليها وعلى ما أمرتما به من الدعوة إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority doubles both tāʾ and nūn in تتبعان; other reported readings vary the doubling, and grammarians disagree whether the light nūn can be emphatic in this dual form or instead marks a negative indicative used as a prohibition or circumstance.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تتبعان بتشديد التاء والنون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Dhakwān lighten the tāʾ and strengthen the nūn; Ibn Dhakwān also transmits the reverse pattern, while another group lightens the tāʾ and leaves the nūn still.
rows.anchor: وابن عباس وابن زكوان بتخفيف التاء وشد النون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads جوزنا with a doubled wāw; he and Qatāda also read فاتبعهم with a doubled tāʾ, while the majority has the fourth-form فأتبعهم.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحسن وجوزنا بتشديد الواو

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari distinguishes جاوز from جوز, citing poetry and arguing that the construction with Israel requires the bāʾ when it means crossing through the sea.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وليس من جوز الذي في بيت الأعشى

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥawfi says تبع and اتبع have the same meaning; Zamakhshari explains the latter as catching up, and al-Lawāmiʿ contrasts merely walking behind with overtaking.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: تبع واتبع بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unspecified report gives Pharaoh's army as 1.6 million, with other estimates also mentioned.
rows.anchor: وجنود فرعون قيل: ألف ألف وستمائة ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading وعدوا on the pattern علو is also reported; the word derives from hostile transgression, and Pharaoh's pursuit happened as Israel crossed the sea.
rows.anchor: وعدوا وعدوا من العدوان، واتباع فرعون هو في مجاوزة البحر

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A narrative says Pharaoh claimed the sea split by his authority; Gabriel approached on a female horse, Pharaoh's stallion followed, and the troops entered, while Michael drove them all into the sea before it closed over them.
rows.anchor: روي أن فرعون لما انتهى إلى البحر فوجده قد انفرق ومضى فيه بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayhi and al-Kisāʾī deny that the light nūn of emphasis enters this dual construction; Yūnus and al-Farrāʾ allow it.
rows.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه والكسائي أنها لا تدخل هنا الخفيفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Those ignorant of God's way are identified either as Pharaoh and his people or as people who demand a judgment before its time.
rows.anchor: والذين لا يعلمون فرعون وقومه قاله: ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority reads أنه with fatḥ, treating an omitted preposition as understood; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read kasra as a new statement, apposition, or implied quotation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أنه بفتح الهمزة على حذف الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shocked Pharaoh repeats the confession in three forms, either stumbling in terror or hoping intensely for acceptance; it is refused because belief after seeing death comes too late.
rows.anchor: ولما لحقه من الدهش ما لحقه كرر المعنى بثلاث عبارات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say Pharaoh spoke when drowning had reached his throat; another view says he spoke after drowning had overcome him inwardly.
rows.anchor: قيل: قال ذلك حين ألجمه الغرق. وقيل: بعد أن غرق في نفسه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Zamakhshari rejects the story that Gabriel stuffed sea mud into Pharaoh's mouth to block his faith: belief is in the heart, as with a mute person, and wishing a disbeliever to remain faithless is itself disbelief.
rows.anchor: وأما ما يضم إليه من قولهم خشيت أن تدركه رحمة الله تعالى فمن زيادات الباهتين لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke beginning آلآن is apparently God's speech through an angel, identified variously as Gabriel, Michael, or another; another view makes it Pharaoh's own inner speech.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: آلآن إلى آخره من كلام الله له على لسان ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Treating فاليوم ننجيك as a question of threat is unlikely because it requires an omitted interrogative hamza and makes the purpose clause about becoming a sign incoherent.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو استفهام فيه تهديد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ننجيك as casting Pharaoh onto elevated dry ground and بدن as his armor, said to be a uniquely splendid pearl cuirass; other views name gold or iron armor with gold chains.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ننجيك نلقيك بنجوة من الأرض وهي المكان المرتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two poetic lines use الأبدان and بدني for armor, supporting the interpretation of Pharaoh's body as his armor.
rows.anchor: ترى الأبدان فيها مسبغات ... على الأبطال والكلب الحصينا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations take بدن as an unclothed and unarmed corpse for humiliation, a body recovered intact, or a lifeless corpse; Mujāhid is named for the last.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بدنا بلا روح قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Further views understand the phrase as removing Pharaoh from his kingdom alone, casting him into the sea, leaving him to drown, making him a sign, drowning him, or hastening his destruction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نتركك حتى تغرق، والنجاء الترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes بدن as Pharaoh's recognizable appearance; if it means his corpse, the phrase is emphatic like saying someone spoke with his tongue or came in person.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى ببدنك بصورتك التي تعرف بها

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads ننجيك with a lightened form, the present of أنجى.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب: ننجيك مخففا مضارع أنجى

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy, Ibn al-Sumayqa, Yazīd al-Barbarī, and a report from Ibn Masʿūd read ننحيك with ḥāʾ, meaning cast to the side of the sea; Kaʿb says the sea threw him ashore like a bull.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي، وابن السميقع، ويزيد البربري: ننحيك بالحاء المهملة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Ḥanīfa reads بأبدانك, either referring to Pharaoh's armor or using each body part as a body, like saying his temples went gray.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة: بأبدانك أي بدروعك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn al-Sumayqa read بندائك instead of ببدنك, referring to Pharaoh's useless call of faith or his proclamations to his people.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود، وابن السميقع: بندائك مكان ببدنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those left behind may mean the Israelites, who had thought Pharaoh too mighty to drown and saw his corpse on their route; alternatively it means later generations or surviving Egyptians, with an opening-lām reading referring to future tyrants.
rows.anchor: لمن وراءك علامة وهم بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting Pharaoh's destruction, the passage recalls God's favor to Israel: He chose excellent dwellings for them after they were driven from their homes in fear of Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: إذ كان بنو إسرائيل قد أخرجوا من مساكنهم خائفين من فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent referent is the Israelites who believed Moses and survived the drowning, as the passage's sequence indicates; another view identifies the tribes present with the Prophet, Qurayẓa, Naḍīr, and Qaynuqāʿ.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن بني إسرائيل هم الذين كانوا آمنوا بموسى ونجوا من الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مبوأ صدق is grammatically a second object of بوأنا, though it may instead be a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وانتصب مبوأ صدق على أنه مفعول ثان لبوأنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrase means honor and favor, as in مقعد صدق; other views take it as a place where a promise proved true, a gift of charity, or a dwelling that fulfilled its residents' hopes.
rows.anchor: ومعنى صدق أي: فضل وكرامة ومنه في مقعد صدق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A variant reads لمن خلقك, meaning God makes Pharaoh a sign among His servants; another explanation says the isolated body prevents people from claiming a self-proclaimed deity cannot die and displays God's power.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: لمن خلقك من الخلق وهو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes many people literally as all people; Muqātil instead identifies the heedless as Meccans who fail to reflect on signs of divine unity and other attributes, a warning within the report.
rows.anchor: قاله الحسن. وقال مقاتل من أهل مكة عن آياتنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other glosses call it a sound, pleasing dwelling. Ibn ʿAbbās identifies it as Jordan and Palestine; al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Zayd, and Qatāda say Syria and Jerusalem; Muqātil says Jerusalem; al-Ḍaḥḥāk also gives Egypt or Egypt and Syria.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: هو الأردن وفلسطين. وقال الضحاك وابن زيد، وقتادة: الشام وبيت المقدس

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers Syria and Jerusalem because the Israelites did not return to Egypt, and says the Quran supports this identification.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والأصح أنه الشام وبيت المقدس بحسب ما حفظ من أنهم لم يعودوا إلى مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bequest may mean the gardens, springs, and other property left by the Egyptians, or the broader condition of blessing even if it was not confined to one territory; a Medina-to-Syria location is suggested if the Israelite referent is the Prophet's contemporaries.
rows.anchor: وأورثناها بني إسرائيل يعني ما ترك القبط من جنات وعيون وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also supplied them with pleasant foods or lawful foods; they initially followed one way with Moses, then divided after knowledge of the Torah came, which is blameworthy because knowledge became the cause of their schisms.
rows.anchor: وهي: المآكل المستلذات، أو الحلال، فما اختلفوا أي: كانوا على ملة واحدة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, knowledge means Muḥammad: the Torah foretold his mission and the Jews had once invoked him for victory, but some rejected him because they expected a descendant of Jacob rather than Ishmael; ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his followers believed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العلم بمعنى المعلوم، وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes knowledge as the Quran: people differed over whether it came from Muḥammad or God, and whether it was for them or only the Arabs; some accepted it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: العلم القرآن، واختلافهم قول بعضهم هو من كلام محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disagreement cannot be resolved in this world; God will judge it at the Resurrection and distinguish the right from the false.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف لا يمكن زواله في الدنيا، وأنه تعالى يقضي فيه في الآخرة
